decisions.contract: ctx must be a live EVP_MD_CTX whose md_data is a writable SHA_CTX, exclusively borrowed for the call.
what_was_checked: The installing table is EVP_ORIG_GLOBAL with ctx_size == 0 (legacy_md), so evp_md_init_internal takes the legacy arm only for EVP_ORIG_METH or EVP_MD_CTX_FLAG_NO_INIT (src/evp/digest.rs:2146); the NO_INIT arm returns at :2334 before init is called. The crate's own initialise path therefore never supplies the block.

That does NOT establish the precondition. The exported EVP_MD_meth_get_init (src/evp/digest.rs:1565; exported at artifacts/phase2/libcrypto.ld:1886) returns this callback pointer to any C caller. Its documented contract is only that the getter retrieves the data supplied to EVP_MD_meth_set_* (doc/man3/EVP_MD_meth_new.pod:165-169); it says nothing about the caller's md_data.

A caller can pass EVP_MD_CTX_new(), which zero-fills the block (src/evp/digest.rs:1899-1907), so md_data is NULL. The callback would dereference/write NULL. There is no external ABI contract that makes md_data writable for a context the caller chooses.

The earlier contract's claim that the callback is 'only reachable if a caller made this table its own legacy method with a matching ctx_size, which no exported entry point does' was inaccurate; the exported getter reaches the callback without re-origining the table. The contract was rewritten to state the real witness.

decisions.satisfied_criterion: criterion 2 via the documented public UI_METHOD C ABI
decisions.contract: pass writable for pass_size; pass_len writable; prompt_info NULL or NUL-terminated; ui_method NULL or a live UI_METHOD that outlives the call; ui_data whatever that method's callbacks expect.
precondition_to_abi_mapping: live UI_METHOD/outlives the call: UI_METHOD is opaque (include/openssl/ui.h:293-294), created only by the exported UI_create_method, and installed borrowed by the public OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_set_passphrase_ui / OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_passphrase_ui (doc/man3/OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_new_for_pkey.pod, doc/man3/OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey.pod) through ossl_pw_set_ui_method (src/passphrase.rs:375). The application owns the lifetime, as it does for every borrowed C API object.
callbacks valid: only the exported UI_method_set_* family installs them (include/openssl/ui.h:339-357), so the vtable layout and member types are the public ABI's.

callback semantics: opener/writer/flusher/reader/closer return 0 on error, 1 on success, -1 for out-of-band events, and only the flusher/reader may return -1 (doc/man3/UI_create_method.pod). UI_process (src/ui/ui_lib.rs:1411) handles exactly those three answers.

reader result extent: a reader sets its answer with UI_set_result/UI_set_result_ex, which rejects a length outside result_minsize..result_maxsize (doc/man3/UI_STRING.pod; src/ui/ui_lib.rs:2187). do_ui_passphrase installs pass_size as the maxsize, so UI_get_result_length cannot exceed the pass extent.
prompt constructor: when present it must return an OPENSSL_malloc-allocated string for OPENSSL_free (crypto/ui/ui_local.h, ui_construct_prompt comment). UiScratch::drop performs exactly that release.

ui_data: UI_add_user_data stores the application pointer without duplication; the public UI documentation says the caller owns it (doc/man3/UI_new.pod, UI_add_user_data). No stricter property is required.
decisions.why_no_extra_requirement: do_ui_passphrase only passes the method to UI_set_method, its data to UI_add_user_data, and the callback-driven UI_construct_prompt/UI_process/UI_get_result_length calls. Each requirement is one of the bullets above; no crate-private validation of the UI_METHOD object is required beyond 'it is a UI_METHOD from the public API, alive for the call'. An application that violates the published callback contract is outside the ABI, exactly as with any public OpenSSL callback.
